classification_signals: The document is titled '11 AUDITORY PERCEPTION AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE', indicating it is likely a chapter in a larger work. It extensively synthesizes existing research, standards (ISO, ANSI), and theoretical concepts across various aspects of audition, including thresholds, discrimination, loudness, masking, critical bands, pitch, timbre, sound quality, perceived duration, spatial perception, and hearing loss. It includes numerous figures and tables adapted from other published works (e.g., ISO, ANSI, Scharf, Zwicker, Fastl, Egan, Hake, Olson, Wightman, Green, Blauert, Levitt, Webster, Elliott, Feddersen, Mills, Letowski, Miskiewicz, Bismarck, Yamashita, Ptratt, Doak, Gabrielsson, Sjögren, Lindström, Slot, Neuhoff, McBeath, Harrell, Emanuel). There are no methods, results, or discussion sections presenting new empirical data from the authors.
title: AUDITORY PERCEPTION AND COGNITIVE PERFORMANCE
authors: Angélique A. Scharine et al., Unknown Year

findings.antecedent: Auditory sensation (basic physical characteristics of sound)
findings.consequent: Sound discrimination and classification (sensation); Sound recognition and identification (perception)
findings.quote: Auditory sensation forms the basis for discrimination between two or more sounds and may lead to some forms of sound classification (e.g., labeling sounds as pleasant or unpleasant). However, auditory sensation does not involve sound recognition, which requires a higher level of cognitive processing of the auditory stimuli. This higher level processing forms a conceptual interpretation of the auditory stimulus and is referred to as auditory perception.

findings.antecedent: Level of cognitive processing (of auditory stimuli)
findings.consequent: Auditory perception (classification, recognition, identification, reasoning, mental synthesis, concept building)
findings.quote: Depending on the level of cognitive processing, auditory perception may involve processes of sound classification, e.g., on speech and non-speech sounds, sound recognition, or sound identification. More complex cognitive processing also may include acts of reasoning, selection, mental synthesis, and concept building involving auditory stimuli but extends beyond the realm of audition.

findings.consequent: Detection threshold (sensation and perception of sound)
findings.quote: An auditory stimulus arriving at the auditory system needs to exceed a certain level of stimulation to cause the temporary changes in the state of the system that result in the sensation and perception of sound.

findings.antecedent: Frequency, duration, and spectral complexity of auditory stimulus
findings.quote: The minimum level of stimulation required to evoke a physiologic response from the auditory system is called the threshold of hearing or detection threshold and depends on the frequency, duration, and spectral complexity of the stimulus.
Normal daily variability of the threshold of hearing can be assumed to be 6 dB or less.

findings.antecedent: Repeated measures of hearing threshold (4000 Hz)
findings.quote: Delany (1970) and Robinson (1986) used a Bekesy tracing procedure... and both reported an average standard deviation in the order of 5 dB at 4000 Hertz (Hz) for repeated measures of the threshold of hearing on the same person.

findings.consequent: Within-subject variability (standard deviation) of hearing threshold
findings.quote: Henry et al. (2001) used insert earphones ER-4B... and reported average within subject standard deviations between 1.9 dB and 5.3 dB depending on the stimulus frequency.

findings.antecedent: Listener's familiarity, interest, attention, experience, procedural effects
findings.quote: it is useful to differentiate between the physiological threshold defined by the inherent physiological abilities of the listener and the cognitive threshold limited by the listener's familiarity with the stimuli, interest in and attention to the task, experience with existing set of circumstances, and the numerous procedural effects in eliciting the listener's response
The cognitive thresholds can be made close to the physiological thresholds by an appropriate amount and type of training

findings.antecedent: Low and middle frequencies; increasing stimulus frequency
findings.consequent: Inter-subject variability (standard deviation) of hearing threshold
findings.quote: inter-subject (between-subject) standard deviations ranging from 3 dB to 6 dB were reported for low and middle frequencies in a number of studies (Moller and Pedersen, 2004) and the inter-subject data variability tends to increase with stimulus frequency.
The binaural thresholds of hearing shown in Figure 11-1 and Table 11-1 are approximately 2 dB lower than the corresponding monaural thresholds if both ears have similar sensitivity
Their audibility does not vary much among individuals and depends primarily on the mechanical properties of the ear.
